name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_Ctor
summary: Derived-class constructor: runs the shared base constructor 0x005D451C, installs vtable 0x00783F64 at +0xC4 and constructs the two 4-byte elements that follow it, then returns the object base.
evidence: Disassembly 0x5D658C-0x5D65AC: `bl 0x5D451C` (shared base constructor), `str r1,[r0],#0xC4` installs vtable 0x00783F64 at +0xC4, `blx std_ConstructArray(+0xC4, 0x006F0958, 4, 2)`, `sub r0,r0,#0xC4` returns the base. The old 'InitValuePair' described only the two 4-byte elements and missed the base-ctor + vtable install, so this is a constructor.

name: Gfx_ScreenViews_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the screen-views collection: builds three sub-arrays (16 x 0x10, 32 x 0x1C, 36 x 0x2C), installs the base vtable 0x00782234 at +0xAB0 with a 0xFF sentinel at +0xAB8, resets every entry and returns the base pointer.
evidence: Disassembly shows a full constructor, not a std_ConstructArray wrapper: three std_ConstructArray calls (0x001F2BA4 x16, 0x001C9F9C x32, 0x002B7C44 x36), `str r2,[r0,#0x630]!` writes base vtable 0x00782234 at +0xAB0, then three reset loops call Gfx_ScreenViewEntry_ResetShort (0x001F2AD4) and Gfx_ScreenViewEntry_Reset (0x001C9D9C). Named siblings Gfx_ScreenViews_InitBuffers (0x006227CC) and Gfx_ScreenView_ResetCollections (0x00622C30) fix the family.

name: maybe_Field_TestAreaOverlapA
signature: u32 maybe_Field_TestAreaOverlapA(void* owner, void* point, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, float* offset)
summary: Builds a four-corner box from a point (+0x4C/+0x50/+0x54/+0x58) plus the caller's offset and tests it against a list of field objects; the 4 x 8-byte corner array is constructed with the no-op constructor 0x006F56F4 and the test itself runs in this function.
evidence: 0x006F56F4 is a bare `bx lr` stub, so the previous 'tail call to the real box test at 0x006F56F4' reading is wrong - that address is only the element constructor passed to std_ConstructArray(sp+0x30, 0x006F56F4, 8, 4) and the function continues afterwards. Named callers are Field_Marker_TestOverlap (0.60) and maybe_Field_Placement_TestAreaA/B/C, so the Gimmick prefix is unsupported.

name: maybe_Field_TestAreaOverlapB
signature: u32 maybe_Field_TestAreaOverlapB(void* owner, void* point, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, float* offset)
summary: Sibling of 0x00652F48: builds the same four-corner box from the point in argument 2 plus the caller's offset and tests it against a list of field objects; only the argument positions differ.
evidence: Same shape as 0x00652F48 with the point in r1 instead of the 5th stack argument, and the same no-op element constructor 0x006F56F4 (`bx lr`), so the 'zone test at 0x006F56F4' reading is wrong. The only caller is maybe_Field_Marker_UpdateScreenOffset, so the Gimmick prefix is unsupported and the box/zone distinction cannot be proven.

name: maybe_StaticInit_Array20x8_7ECDA8
summary: Global static initialiser: builds a 20-entry, 8-byte table in the static buffer at 0x007ECDA8 with the zeroing element constructor 0x00146A74 and clears the tail words at +0xA0..+0xAC.
evidence: No caller and no callee; the readable body is empty and the linear disassembly loses ARM/Thumb sync at 0x00678B54 (the bytes 10 40 2d e9 are `push {r4,lr}` but are decoded as Thumb), so only the header's raw-disassembly note survives. The Container_ prefix claimed a container method; this is a global static initialiser.

name: maybe_Os_InitExclusiveAccessTable
summary: Early-boot initialiser: fills the capability/count block at 0x007F2630, clears the flags at 0x007B00A4 and 0x007F2A58, takes the exclusive-access words with LDREX/STREX and fills them with 0xFFFFFFFF, then constructs eight 0x18-byte entries at +0x2C.
evidence: Unchanged reading. The element constructor 0x0051CBCC sits inside the nn::err block (FACTS: 0x0051BA34..0x0051CD40), so the eight 0x18-byte entries may be fatal-error records rather than an owner table, and the 0x007B00A4 flag is shared with Gfx_OpenGpuChannel/Gfx_ShutdownChannel. Still ambiguous.

name: maybe_Data_InitPairRecords
summary: Stores the id twice and -1 at self+0/+4/+8, then constructs two 0x20-byte records in the global buffer 0x007EF0F4 with the zeroing constructor 0x00509B1C and registers the empty stub 0x00146AF4 as their destructor.
evidence: Disassembly confirms `str r1,[r0]` / `stm r3,{r1,r2}` (self[0]=self[1]=id, self[2]=-1) then std_ConstructArray(0x007EF0F4, 0x00509B1C, 0x20, 2). 0x007EF0F4 is 0x007EF0E8+0xC, the monitor Gfx_ShutdownChannelLocked locks, so the pair is Gfx-owned, but the record type is still unknown and the Data_ prefix stays vague.

name: maybe_Os_InitListRegistry
summary: Initialises the ordered-list registry: constructs its element array, clears the monitor word at 0x007E793C, initialises that critical section and registers the empty stub 0x00509A18 as its static destructor.
evidence: Disassembly: `str r0,[0x007E793C]` then `bl Os_InitCriticalSection(0x007E793C)` - the same monitor maybe_Os_InsertListNodeByKey (0x0010CCB0) locks before walking the ordered list at 0x007AE954 - then a tail call to the empty stub 0x00509A18 (`bx lr`). So it initialises the list registry, not a container.

name: maybe_StaticInit_Array32x16_7E7BE0
summary: Global static initialiser: constructs 0x20 elements of 0x10 bytes at the static buffer 0x007E7BE0 with the zeroing element constructor 0x005052A4 and then re-points the table base.
evidence: No caller; the readable body is empty and the linear disassembly loses ARM/Thumb sync at 0x0069A090 (bytes f0 41 2d e9 are `push {r4-r8,lr}` but are decoded as Thumb), so only the header's raw-disassembly note survives. 0x007E7BE0 is also referenced by Fs_RegisterMountByName/Fs_UnmountByName, which hints at a mount table, but the element type 0x005052A4 is a plain 3-word zeroing constructor.

name: maybe_StaticInit_7AF0AC
summary: Global static initialiser: constructs an element array, then writes 0 and a 1 flag byte at 0x007AF0AC and two zero words at 0x007AF0B4, and registers the empty stub 0x00509AE4 as their static destructor.
evidence: Disassembly: std_ConstructArray, then `str r4,[0x007AF0AC]` / `strb r1,[r0,#4]` (1) and `str r4,[0x007AF0B4]` / `str r4,[r0,#4]`, then a tail call to the empty stub 0x00509AE4 (`bx lr`). The only caller (Ui_SakusenWindow_PushCommandForCursor) does not fit a static initialiser, so the subsystem is unknown and the address is kept in the name.

name: maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_InitTables
summary: Static initialiser of the sequence-player tables: constructs the element array, clears the state words at +0x38..+0x44, writes the table-base pointers into the globals at 0x007E7518, 0x007AE8BC and 0x00781998, then tail-calls the named Sound_SeqPlayer_InitVoiceMap.
evidence: Disassembly ends with `b #0x54FADC`, the named Sound_SeqPlayer_InitVoiceMap, and the globals it fills (0x007E7518 = 0x00146A64, 0x007AE8BC, 0x00781998) are the sequence-player tables. The Container_ prefix was wrong.

name: maybe_Gfx_HandleVBlank
summary: Display/vblank event handler: takes the display lock, sends the request word, and when the frame-done bit 0x20 is clear re-arms the display state and submits a 0x1000-byte command block through maybe_Gfx_ServiceDisplayTransfer.
evidence: The entry condition is still a damaged `in_ZR` register, so the guard cannot be trusted; the rest is consistent - Svc_SendRequestWord, Os_UnlockScheduler, the frame-done test `(func_00113954() & 0x20) == 0` and the 0x1000-byte block handed to maybe_Gfx_ServiceDisplayTransfer. Kept honest as maybe_.

name: maybe_Gfx_InitFrameBuffers
signature: int maybe_Gfx_InitFrameBuffers(void* set, unsigned int size)
summary: One-shot display-buffer setup guarded by the flag at 0x007AEA70: allocates `size` bytes, copies the 0x2b0-byte command block into the set and derives the five sub-buffer pointers at 0, 0xa8, 0x108, 0x158 and 0x238.
evidence: The body only moves the six Os_SendIpcQuery6 results and the 0x2b0-byte block into the set and derives five sub-buffer offsets; the framebuffer reading still rests on the paired teardown 0x10C0D8 (called from maybe_Gfx_ReleaseRenderer) and on the caller maybe_Os_ShutdownSyncObject, neither of which is confidently named.

name: Gfx_ShutdownChannelLocked
summary: Locked wrapper around the GPU channel teardown: takes the monitor at 0x007EF0E8, calls the named Gfx_ShutdownChannel, releases the monitor and returns 0.
evidence: The body is exactly Os_LockMonitor(0x007EF0E8) / Gfx_ShutdownChannel() / unlock / return 0 - the same lock-call-unlock triple Gfx_ShutdownGlobalState (0x001073BC) inlines - and the callee is now the named Gfx_ShutdownChannel (0x0010BA40), so the 'locked wrapper' reading is certain.

name: Os_InsertListNodeByKey
summary: Inserts a node into the global ordered list at 0x007AE954 (head +4, tail +8) sorted by the 32-bit key at node+0x10, under the monitor at 0x007E793C, patching both link directions.
evidence: The body is a complete sorted insert: it walks the list from 0x007AE954+4 comparing node[4] (the key at +0x10), patches *piVar4 and piVar4[4] in both directions and updates the tail at +8, all under Os_LockMonitor(0x007E793C). Callers Snd_OpenDspService and Mem_MapSharedBlock both register a node in that shared registry.

name: Gfx_IpcLockedQuery
summary: Takes the display driver lock, issues the GPU IPC command 0x1010000 with one argument and releases the lock, returning the reply word.
evidence: The body is the same lock/call/unlock triple as the sibling Gfx_IpcLockedSend2 (0x0010DA38), with the now-named GPU IPC stub Gfx_IpcCmd1010000 as its only callee; the lock pair func_00119BA8/Os_UnlockScheduler is shared with the other Gfx IPC wrappers.

name: Gfx_IpcLockedSend2
summary: Sends a two-word request on the GPU IPC channel with the scheduler lock held and returns the reply.
evidence: The body is func_00119BA8() / Gfx_IpcCmd4F0080(arg1,arg2) / Os_UnlockScheduler() / return - the same wrapper shape as Gfx_IpcLockedQuery (0x0010D40C), with the now-named Gfx_IpcCmd4F0080 as the only callee.

name: Snd_RestoreChannelState
summary: Re-applies a saved channel state to the driver context 0x007EF414: gain, per-unit gain/active/ADPCM state for both units, pan, format, length, output select, rate, volume and level, then clears the saved pending word at +0x2C.
evidence: Every setter it calls is now a named Snd_Set* member of the same family (Snd_SetUnitActive, Snd_SetChannelRate, Snd_SetChannelLength, maybe_Snd_SetChannelGain/Format/AdpcmState/UnitGain/Level), and it writes them from the saved record in a fixed order before clearing state->f_2C - the mirror of the save half at 0x112A9C.

name: Gfx_InitDrawState
summary: One-shot initialisation of the shared GPU draw-state object: opens the gsp::Gpu session, publishes the handle, clears the 28-word state block at 0x007A1C40 and installs it as the singleton's f_1c, then starts the IPC worker.
evidence: The caller is the named Gfx_InitializeContext (0x00109FB0), the one-shot flag is 0x007AF178, the handle comes from the 'gsp::Gpu' literal at 0x007AF17C, and the 28-word block at 0x007A1C40 is installed as singleton->f_1c - the slot maybe_Gfx_ExchangeSlotValue hands out.

name: maybe_Snd_SetSuspendState
signature: void maybe_Snd_SetSuspendState(unsigned int suspend, void* state)
summary: Level-triggered suspend/resume switch: when the stored flag at state+3 is set it clears it and calls Snd_RequestResume, otherwise it sets the flag and calls Snd_RequestSuspend; the two 'already in that state' results 0xD8A02A05/0xD9001BF7 are accepted and a negative result goes to the error reporter.
evidence: The entry condition is a damaged `in_ZR` register, so the guard cannot be trusted; the two branches call the named Snd_RequestResume/Snd_RequestSuspend and accept the two 'already in that state' results. Kept honest as maybe_.

name: Snd_SendIpcSuspend
signature: unsigned int Snd_SendIpcSuspend(unsigned int* session, unsigned int value, unsigned char mode)
summary: IPC stub for driver command 0x16 (header word 0x00160042): stores the mode byte, the value and a zero word in the thread-local block, sends svc 0x32 and returns the reply.
evidence: The header word 0x00160042 encodes driver command 0x16 with one parameter, and the only named caller Snd_RequestSuspend (0x001193DC) passes mode 0 and compares the reply against the two 'already suspended/resumed' results; the second caller (maybe_Gfx_InitDrawState) uses the same stub during driver init.

name: maybe_Queue_SubmitEntry
summary: Appends a buffer entry to the owner's submission chain, publishes it with a memory barrier and either pushes it to the OS queue or the ring buffer, then assigns and returns the next sequence number.
evidence: The body is a damaged fragment that reads the owner and flags from unaff_r4/r5/r7, and the header's '2920 Thumb bytes' does not match the 20-statement body, so the decompilation cannot be trusted. The callers span Container_ForEachPair, Gfx_InitCommandLists, Gfx_InitSubsystems and Sound_WaveArchive_LoadAndCache, so the Snd_ prefix was unsupported; only the queue/ring-buffer submit shape is visible.

name: Sound_Channel_ApplyMaskedWord
summary: When the channel block is initialised and no slot is owned, acquires the driver slot, submits a one-word masked block carrying the byte-swapped word from self+4 and records the slot in the owner byte.
evidence: The only caller is the named Sound_Player_StartSlotTrack (0x0054F2EC), and the body acquires the driver slot (func_00516ECC) then writes the one-word masked block {mask 2, byteswapped self+4} through the named Sound_Channel_WriteParamBlock, recording the slot in self->f_d.

name: Sound_Channel_ReleaseSlot
summary: Stops a channel's parameter block: submits the mask-1 block, releases the driver slot with 0x516EEC, marks the owner byte 0xFF and clears the four channel words.
evidence: The only caller is the named Sound_Player_StopSlot (0x0054F6D0); the body writes the mask-1 block, releases the driver slot with func_00516EEC, sets self+0xD = 0xFF and clears self[0..3]. 'ClearParamRamp' assumed the block holds a ramp, which nothing in the body supports - the release is what it does.

name: Snd_SetChannelMaskedFields
signature: unsigned int Snd_SetChannelMaskedFields(void* buf, int index, unsigned short* info)
summary: Copies a mask-selected set of fields from a descriptor into one 0x14-byte channel record (bit0 one halfword, bit1 one word, bit2 five halfwords) and sets the dirty bit 0x400 for unit 0 or 0x800 for unit 1.
evidence: The two callers are the channel-unit reset paths (maybe_Snd_ResetChannelUnitsInPlace, maybe_Snd_ResetChannelUnitsToDefault), and the body copies the mask-selected fields into the 0x14-byte record under the driver lock (func_0011E99C/func_0011E9A8), OR-ing the mask into +0x2C and setting the dirty bits 0x400/0x800.

name: maybe_Os_PerfSample_Loop
summary: One sampling pass of the SDK timing loop: for each configured entry it reads the system tick, sleeps and accumulates elapsed microseconds against the 1,000,000 constant, stopping early at the 0x3FE marker, then sets the state word at 0x007B00E0 to 3 or 0.
evidence: The 0x000F4240 (1,000,000) constant, the svc 0x28 (svcGetSystemTick) reads and the 0x007F2644/0x007B0080 tables support the sampling reading, but the named caller Gfx_OpenGpuChannel and the timer helpers do not mention profiling, so the purpose stays a hypothesis.

name: Os_IpcSendCommand19
summary: Sends IPC command 0x19 (thread-local command word 0x00190040) with one parameter on the session at 0x007B2D2C and returns the reply word from TLS+0x84.
evidence: The TLS header word 0x00190040 encodes IPC command 0x19 with one parameter and the reply is read back from TLS+0x84 after svc 0x32; the doc's callers (Fs_ReadRecordBlock, maybe_Save_CheckReadState) place it in the file/save I/O path, so it is a command stub, not a thread-local store.

name: Math_AlignUp
signature: u32 Math_AlignUp(int stream, int offset, int extra)
summary: Rounds extra+offset up to the stream's alignment (field +4) by forwarding to the shared align helper 0x0011CFAC; Ghidra dropped the real return value and shows only the extraout_r1 copy.
evidence: The body is a one-line forward to the shared align helper 0x0011CFAC with (extra+offset, stream->f_4); Ghidra lost the return register (extraout_r1), but the caller Fs_ReadRecordBlock uses the result to compute the next record offset, which fixes the align-up reading.

name: Item_SelectCategoryById
summary: Selects an item-window category: resolves the item window from the field manager and, when it has no category yet (byte +0x398 == 0xFF), forwards the category to the named Item_SelectCategory.
evidence: The callee is the named Item_SelectCategory (0x002555F4), which stores the category at window+0x398 and clears the per-entry filter flags; the guard func_00636B34 is `ldrb r0,[r0,#0x398]; cmp r0,#0xFF; moveq r0,#1`, i.e. the same 'no category yet' test, so the wrapper only resolves the window and forwards.

name: Script_LazyCreateHelperObject
summary: Lazily creates a 0x14-byte helper object owned by self (vtable 0x00780278), stores the value at +0xC and the back-pointer at +0x10, and returns the cached object.
evidence: Both callers are named script-VM helpers (Script_Closure_BindEnv 0x006BAA68, Script_Vm_PushRootTable 0x006BDE24); the body allocates 0x14 bytes once, stamps vtable 0x00780278, stores the value at +0xC and the back-pointer at +0x10, and returns the cached pointer.

name: Script_BindEnvOk
summary: Thin script-native status wrapper: calls the named Script_Closure_BindEnv and returns 1 for a non-negative result, 0xFFFFFFFF otherwise.
evidence: The only callee is now the named Script_Closure_BindEnv, and the 1/-1 convention matches the neighbouring script-native wrappers; what the native exposes to scripts is still unknown, but the wrapper shape is certain.

name: Event_ActorSlot_PlayTalkMotion
summary: Resolves an event actor slot by index, resolves its handle and asks the actor to play the talk motion with the given index through the named Field_Actor_PlayTalkMotionFromTable.
evidence: The body bounds-checks actorIndex against the event actor slots (work+8->+0x6C, f_430/f_434 stride 0x10), resolves the handle with 0x005F5818 (a handle-table lookup) and calls the now-named Field_Actor_PlayTalkMotionFromTable (0x005F5B94) with the second argument. Nothing touches a sound object, so Sound_PlayActorSeByIndex was wrong.

name: Sq_RegisterTableMembers
summary: Finishes a table-style native registration: opens the member group with the descriptor at 0x0015C720, builds the member array from the stack with the descriptor at 0x0015C66C and closes the registration.
evidence: The three calls are the begin/push/end steps of a Squirrel table registration (func_006BD2F0 with 0x0015C720, Sq_NewArrayFromStack with 0x0015C66C, Script_SetSlotFromStackAlt), and the neighbouring functions are the named script-VM helpers; the descriptors themselves are not decoded.

name: maybe_Script_ReturnZeroStub2
summary: Placeholder script native: performs the VM's stack-slot bookkeeping (Script_SetSlotFromStackAlt) and returns 0.
evidence: The only callee is the VM helper Script_SetSlotFromStackAlt; there is no caller and no distinguishable behaviour, so it stays an honest stub name.

name: Menu_Equip_SetMemberVisibility
summary: Forwards a member id and a visibility value to the named Menu_Equip_SetMemberVisibilityFlag, which stores the value at member+0x12E4 and updates the equipped-model node visibility.
evidence: The only callee is the named Menu_Equip_SetMemberVisibilityFlag (0x0023CDE0), which stores the value at member+0x12E4 and calls Model_Equip_UpdateNodeVisibility; this wrapper only resolves the overlay manager from work+8->+0x48 and forwards (memberId, value), so Field_SetGadgetParam named the wrong subsystem.

name: Actor_ShowEquipPartA
summary: For actors of the expected runtime type, looks up the equipped item recorded in the component's f_4C and, if the item row is valid, enables the grip node with Model_Equip_SetGripNode(comp,1,0) and sets flag +0x61.
evidence: The item lookup (Item_LookupRecord on comp->f_4C) and the grip-node call show this is equipment-part visibility; the type-id check is still an unlabelled literal, but the Show/Hide pair with 0x00160EB4 (same body, visibility 0, flag cleared) fixes the reading.

name: Actor_HideEquipPartA
summary: Inverse of 0x0016068C: for the same actor type and valid equipped item, disables the grip node with Model_Equip_SetGripNode(comp,0,0) and clears flag +0x61.
evidence: Identical item/grip-node path as 0x0016068C with the visibility argument 0 and the flag cleared, confirming the equip-part Show/Hide pair; the type constant remains unidentified.

name: maybe_Actor_ShowEquipPartB
signature: void maybe_Actor_ShowEquipPartB(void* actor, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 forwarded)
summary: Variant of the equip-part enabler: sets the grip node with Model_Equip_SetGripNode(comp,1,1,...) and sets flag +0x60.
evidence: Same type check and component fetch as 0x0016068C but the second visibility pair (1,1) and flag +0x60; the body is damaged (unaff_r4/r5/r6, in_lr) so the extra arguments stay undecoded and the confidence stays below 0.5.

name: maybe_Actor_HideEquipPartB
signature: void maybe_Actor_HideEquipPartB(void* actor, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 forwarded)
summary: Inverse of 0x00160F14: calls Model_Equip_SetGripNode(comp,0,1,...) and clears flag +0x60.
evidence: Same body as 0x00160F14 with visibility 0 and the flag cleared; the body is damaged (unaff_r4/r5/r6, in_lr) so the extra arguments stay undecoded and the confidence stays below 0.5.

name: Event_ActorSlot_ReleaseEffects
summary: Resolves event actor slot `actorIndex` to its actor and, for mode 2 or 3, calls the named Gfx_Node_ReleaseEffectSlots with 1 or 0.
evidence: The only call is the named Gfx_Node_ReleaseEffectSlots (0x005F747C) with 1 for mode 2 and 0 for mode 3, after the same event-slot bounds check as Event_ActorSlot_PlayTalkMotion (0x00155E40); nothing in the body touches sound.

name: Field_ActorAction_ApplyTransforms
summary: Copies the action's cached transform blocks (self+0x78..+0x94 and +0x98..+0xA4) into the actor's render node actor->f_244[self->f_D8] at +0x5F4..+0x620, and the second block into actor->f_160.
evidence: The body writes self+0x78..+0xD4 into the two actor render nodes at +0x5F4..+0x620 selected by self->f_D8; it has no callee, so it is the transform-copy half of the pair whose full per-frame update is 0x00413938.

name: maybe_Field_ActorAction_Finish
summary: Releases the actor's effect slots with Gfx_Node_ReleaseEffectSlots(actor,1) and then dispatches the actor's virtual +0x88 handler.
evidence: The 40-byte body only releases the effect slots and dispatches actor vtable +0x88; nothing mentions an item box, and the vtable 0x0076B114 also holds 0x003E573C (PlayGondolaNutAnim) and the destructor 0x003E57DC, so the OpenItemBoxAction label was unsupported.

name: Field_ActorAction_Update
summary: Per-frame action update: copies the action's two eight-word transform blocks into the actor's two render nodes (actor->f_244[self->f_D8] and actor->f_160, fields +0x5F4..+0x620), releases the actor's effect slots and then calls actor vtable +0x88.
evidence: The body is the same transform copy as 0x003733D0 but additionally calls the named Gfx_Node_ReleaseEffectSlots and dispatches actor vtable +0x88, so it is the full per-frame update rather than a 'turn' update.

name: Actor_ApplyMotionAndModelSize
summary: Resolves an actor by index and applies the value to its two handle objects depending on the current field mode: mode 1/2 updates the +8 handle through maybe_Gfx_Actor_ApplyMotion, mode 0/2 applies the model size on the +0xC handle.
evidence: The body resolves the actor by index, reads the field mode from func_0062AB3C(work+8) and then calls the named maybe_Gfx_Actor_ApplyMotion on the +8 handle and Gfx_Actor_ApplyModelSize on the +0xC handle; the two callees do different things, so 'SetHandleEnabledBoth' described the call sites rather than one operation.

name: Gfx_EffectPart_BindRelativeTransform
summary: Builds the transform of an effect part relative to another actor (rotation delta from the two 2x2 bases at f_8C..f_98 via acos/cos/sin) and binds it with the named Gfx_EffectPart_BindByName using the part's relative name string at self+4.
evidence: Disassembly 0x162D54-0x162D70 loads r0 = partner (result of 0x005B1208), r1 = self, r2 = self->f_4 relative name and r3 = the 12-float block built on the stack, then `bl 0x5F56A0` = Gfx_EffectPart_BindByName; the readable C dropped three quarters of the call, so the old 'pose copy' reading was wrong.

name: Ui_DialogUpdateQueue
signature: u32 Ui_DialogUpdateQueue(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Page-queue step of the dialog object: when the page list [f_4A4,f_4A8) is empty it sets the pending-page flag at work+0x27220 and runs the embedded handler's vtable +0x14/+0x10 pair; otherwise it pops the next page id and calls the page advance helper func_001675B8.
evidence: The embedded handler at self+0x11C is a vtable object and work+0x27220 is the pending-page flag the message code also uses; the state byte f_48C gates the whole body to the four dialog states 2..5, and the pop path calls func_001675B8 with the popped page id.

name: Container_RemoveFromGlobalList
summary: Removes an object from the global registry vector g_uniqueIdPoolTable, shifts the tail down, unlinks its +0x60 node through func_005647F8 and clears the object's f_E4 flag.
evidence: The body walks g_uniqueIdPoolTable for the object pointer, memmoves the tail down, decrements the end pointer and then unlinks obj+0x60 and clears obj->f_E4; the vtable 0x758B44 places it beside Sound_Emitter_Dtor, Sound_Listener_Dtor and Gfx_Sprite_CreateInstance, which fits a shared object registry.

name: Ui_PopEntryRecord
summary: Pops one byte index from the caller's vector and returns the 8-byte record with that index from the pool reached through 0x007A909C, or null when the index is out of range.
evidence: 17 named callers are all UI window update paths (Ui_UpdateWindowState, Ui_UpdateChildObject, Ui_EquipmentWindow_Update, Ui_JumonWindow_UpdatePartyText, ...), and the body pops one byte index from the vector and resolves it to the 8-byte record in the pool at 0x007A909C; the Container_ prefix was wrong.

name: Ui_GetEntryRecord
summary: Iterator-style accessor: reads the current byte index from the container cursor and returns a pointer to the 8-byte record with that index in the table reached through self+4 (+0x354), or null when out of range; the bounds failure goes to the standard assert path.
evidence: The vtable 0x75DD84 places it beside Ui_CompositeWindow_DtorB and Ui_StatusWindow_UpdateState, and the body resolves the current byte index to the 8-byte record in the table at self+4->+0x354 - the same record layout as Ui_PopEntryRecord (0x002BBA94); the Container_ prefix was wrong.
